decisions.statement: The timers work is scheduled through are handed in so a test needs no wait.
Nothing here reads a clock of its own.
At most one timeout is pending at a time.
Arming again clears the timeout pending rather than adding a second one.
A reset restarts the whole span.
A timeout that fires is no longer pending before the caller's act runs.
A stopped timer is stopped for good.
A reset after a stop arms nothing.
Whether a timer is stopped is answered to the caller.
Arming again after a fire is the caller's own act rather than this module's.
Nothing here knows what the caller's act does.
No caller reaches the handle a timeout is held by.

definition: the one timeout a caller has pending, armed again or stopped
